No kit/livery GLB: only the bare 30k scan in wing-configurator. 'Elise race car livery.obj' (1.48 GB) is in the user's personal Drive folder Livery-Branding, which the service account cannot read (404); asked the user

decision: Car-relative camera recovered for every frame of one whole cycle (Miata: drive-in a60 f1653-1745, hold, drive-out f1838-1972) by fitting the showroom NB Miata GLB's painted-panel silhouette to the game's blue Miata (tools/sil.py, track_car.py, poses.py); focal 1600 px on 2144
why: This menu has no static camera: the car drives in and out with the camera moving. The game's Miata is an NB and the showroom has an NB in the same frame as every kit car, so its outline gives the camera directly. Focal: 1600-2000 fit the close-up frames about equally (IoU cost 0.26 vs 0.28 at 1000), 1600 kept

decision: Each kit car rides the tracked Miata camera, shifted so its wheelbase midpoint sits on the NB's (Corolla +85 mm, Del Sol +73 mm, FR-S +61 mm, NA -9 mm)
why: UG2 lesson: the game parks cars by wheelbase midpoint; the NA test frame landed on the game Miata's wheels

decision: Every car reuses the Miata cycle's capture frames (drive-in f1653-1745, hold f1746-1836, drive-out f1838-1972); only the hold is stretched (72-100 % of real speed) to fit the audio
why: It is the only cycle with a tracked camera (needs a 3D model of the game car), and the Miata is the smallest game car so every kit car covers it. Cost: all cars pass the same stretch of garage

decision: Picture cut to one continuous stretch of the capture's own audio from 16.10 s: each drive-in starts on the game's hard cut (966, 1314, 1653, 1973) and each drive-away on the game's next (1181, 1520, 1840, 2139); ends as the last car has driven off
why: UG2 lesson: cut picture to sound so the game's engine and menu sounds land on each car change with the music unbroken. No clean Get Low track was supplied; the capture's menu music runs under it (tempo ~99 BPM, consistent with Get Low's ~101, not confirmed by ear)

decision: Menu separated into colour (per-pixel minimum over 920 frames) and transmission maps so the kit cars pass under the top band, name plate and stat panel; per-state maps keep the game's stat bars
why: The menu is drawn half transparent over the 3D scene and the car sweeps under it in every drive-in; pasting the render on top would cover the menu

decision: Name plates: Toyota row + the GR COROLLA badge texture from the facelift GLB; the game's own Mazda Miata plate; Honda row + 'del Sol' typeset; 'Scion FR-S' typeset. Logo strip: Toyota, Mazda, Honda lifted from the capture, Scion emblem from Wikimedia Commons. Plate flips 19 frames before the car moves and the strip slides for 28, as measured in the capture
why: UG2 lesson 5: real artwork, lifted where the game has the make. The game has no del Sol or FR-S wordmark and no badge artwork was found for them, so those two words are plain type (flagged to the user)

decision: Stat bars, STYLE points and player name left as the game drew them
why: Not data about our cars; redrawing would mean inventing numbers

decision: 9:16 layout: capture cropped to x 290-1850 (the menu's full width), scaled to 1080x835, on a blurred dark copy of the frame, 60 px above centre
why: Same layout the UG2 reel used; a full-height crop would cut the plate and stats

decision: Light rig rig_garage.json: broad dim ceiling wash, a strip-light row along the lane, weak fills, tail lamps emissive; no shadow catcher
why: Matched by eye to the game's Miata at the hold (frame 1800); the game car's own contact shadow and floor glow stay in the plate and ground the kit car

decision: Wheels of the kit cars get a rotational blur in the composite (each camera-facing wheel disc unwrapped by its plane's homography, blurred 28 degrees around the axle)
why: In this menu the car is rolling the whole time (the garage streams past, the game's wheels turn); static spokes made the car look like it was sliding

decision: Front wheels steered 12 degrees to the right during the approach (to capture frame 1686), straight afterwards
why: UG2 lesson 4: the game turns the front wheels; here it does so only while the car curves in towards the camera (seen on the Miata at f1669), not at the hold

decision: Correction: the capture's music could not be identified as Get Low
why: A second tempo estimate on 16-38 s (bass-band onset autocorrelation) gave no clear peak near 101 BPM (87, 130, 122 all about equal); the earlier 'ive beats' figure of 198.8 was read too generously. Engine and menu sounds sit over the music. Asked the user for the track

decision: Front-wheel steering removed: all frames rendered with the wheels straight (approach frames f1653-1693 re-rendered)
why: User, on seeing the 2-car preview: make sure the wheels are straight. I had steered them 12 degrees during the approach to copy the game's Miata
